clue.text: Current works included in cut

indicators.note: the works are placed inside the word for a current, so this phrase signals one piece going into another

parts.note: a tide is a current of the sea
OPS is short for opuses, musical works

explanation.surface: Some current pieces of work have been shortened by an editor's cut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut' is a butcher's term here: topside is a cut of beef, taken from the top of the leg.
explanation.definitionFit: Topside is a lean joint of beef, i.e. a butcher's cut of meat.

clue.text: It gives a brown coat to animal, fish and insect

parts.note: an ox is a farm animal
the id, or ide, is a freshwater fish
an ant is an insect

explanation.surface: Something seems to be painting an animal, a fish and an insect brown.
explanation.walkthrough: The brown coat is rust: an oxidizing agent gives iron its brown coating.
explanation.definitionFit: An oxidizing agent causes iron to rust, coating it in brown oxide.

clue.text: Too dear to soak

definitions.meaning: to leave it immersed in liquid

explanation.definitionFit: Steep is both an adjective for excessive prices and a verb for immersing in liquid.

clue.text: Subject of Marvell's poem "On a Snotty Nose"?

definitions.text: Subject of Marvell's poem "On a Snotty Nose"?

parts.words: Subject of Marvell's poem "On a Snotty Nose"?
parts.note: Andrew Marvell wrote a poem titled On a Drop of Dew; the clue retitles it as if the drop were the bead hanging from a runny nose

explanation.surface: A mock title for a Marvell poem about a runny nose.
explanation.walkthrough: Marvell's real poem is 'On a Drop of Dew'; a dewdrop is also informal for the drip on the end of a cold nose.
explanation.definitionFit: A dewdrop is a drop of dew and, colloquially, a drip hanging from the nose.

clue.text: "Crikey!" (that's what it says here), "a sea-girt piece of land!"

parts.note: cor is a British exclamation of surprise, like crikey
sic is printed after a quoted word to say it appears exactly so in the original

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims in surprise at spotting a small island surrounded by sea.
explanation.walkthrough: COR is a British exclamation of surprise; SIC is the Latin 'thus' used in print to mean 'written this way'.
explanation.definitionFit: Corsica is a Mediterranean island, land surrounded by sea on all sides.

clue.text: Superior German set over principal fairy

parts.note: ober is German for upper or superior
on can mean placed over or upon something

explanation.surface: A senior German official is put in charge of the head fairy.
explanation.walkthrough: OBER is German for 'upper' (as in Oberammergau).
explanation.definitionFit: Oberon is king of the fairies in A Midsummer Night's Dream, so the chief fairy.

clue.text: Second bungee-jumping artist from the lower orders

indicators.note: jumping suggests the letters of the word bungee leaping about into a new order

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, a crossword artist

explanation.surface: A second bungee-jumping artist comes from the lower classes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bungee-jumping' reads as a sport, but 'jumping' is the anagram signal acting on 'bungee' alone. 'the lower orders' sounds social; here it is biological ranks below genus.
explanation.definitionFit: Subgenera are taxonomic ranks below genus, literally lower classifications of living things.

clue.text: Is crack badly affected by movement of traffic?

indicators.note: badly suggests the letters of is crack are put together wrongly, into another order

explanation.surface: A question whether a drug is badly affected by moving traffic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' rearranges the letters of IS CRACK.
explanation.definitionFit: Being carsick is feeling nauseous from the motion of a vehicle on the road.

clue.text: One man, inebriated, reeling — not English? Not necessarily

definitions.text: One man, inebriated, reeling — not English? Not necessarily

indicators.note: a drunk reels, so this suggests the letters staggering into a new order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: not tells us to leave out a letter from the word before it

explanation.surface: A drunk staggering man may not be English, but that does not follow.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop one E from INEBRIATED, add I and MAN, and 'reeling' rearranges the lot. Something made in Britain needn't be English: it could be Scottish or Welsh.
explanation.definitionFit: Made in Britain describes British manufacture, which could be Welsh or Scottish rather than English.

clue.text: Transmitter man

definitions.meaning: a ..., short for microphone, carries sound to be transmitted

explanation.definitionFit: A mike picks up sound for broadcast, and Mike is a common male name.

clue.text: Avian state born in peculiar surroundings

indicators.note: surroundings tells us the odd word wraps around the other pieces

parts.note: weird means peculiar
to aver is to state firmly
b is the abbreviation for born in genealogies

explanation.surface: A bird-like condition was born in odd circumstances.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Avian' is a noun here: a bird, the weaverbird.
explanation.definitionFit: The weaverbird is an African bird that weaves nests, so a member of the avian world.

clue.text: Practical joker grasps point of ornamental mineral

indicators.note: grasps means holding something within, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a japer plays japes, practical jokes
S, south, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: A prankster grabs the tip of a decorative stone.
explanation.definitionFit: Jasper is an opaque quartz used for ornaments and jewellery.

clue.text: How mysterious to maintain the Queen is anything but!

indicators.note: to maintain is to hold, so the first word holds the second inside it

parts.note: exotic can mean strange and mysterious
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen

explanation.surface: A remark that a mysterious monarch is not mysterious at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'anything but' points back to 'mysterious': exoteric (open, for outsiders) is the opposite of esoteric.
explanation.definitionFit: Exoteric means intended for the general public, the reverse of hidden or arcane.

clue.text: Big, strong, virtuous person emulating Ms Dynamite?

parts.note: ST, saint, is a virtuous person
Ms Dynamite is a British rapper, so copying her means rapping

explanation.surface: A muscular saint is copying a British hip-hop star.
explanation.walkthrough: Ms Dynamite is a British rapper and singer.
explanation.definitionFit: Strapping describes someone big and sturdily built.

clue.text: Organic compound for a largely Cretan police department

indicators.note: largely means most but not all of the word is used

parts.note: Minoan describes ancient Crete
CID is the Criminal Investigation Department of British police

explanation.surface: A complex chemical is ordered for an almost entirely Cretan police team.
explanation.walkthrough: MINOAN loses its last letter to give MINOA; CID is Britain's plain-clothes detective branch.
explanation.definitionFit: Amino acids are organic molecules, the building blocks of proteins.

clue.text: Girl's erstwhile lawyer taken aback by Turkish commander

definitions.note: girl is, with the 's as the verb

indicators.note: taken in, so the commander holds the other piece inside

parts.note: a bey was an Ottoman governor or commander

indicators.note: aback means backwards, so the letters of the lawyer are turned round

parts.note: KC, King's Counsel, was the title of senior barristers before QC under Elizabeth II

explanation.surface: A girl's former lawyer is captured by an Ottoman officer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken aback' looks like 'surprised', but 'aback' turns the lawyer's letters round. KC was an erstwhile title in 2005, when senior barristers were QCs under Elizabeth II.
explanation.definitionFit: Becky is a girl's name, a short form of Rebecca.

clue.text: Russian king in French wood

indicators.note: in places the king inside the French word

parts.note: bois is French for wood
R, rex, is king

explanation.surface: A Russian monarch hides out in a French forest.
explanation.definitionFit: Boris is a typical Russian man's name, as in Godunov or Yeltsin.

clue.text: Cover story finished first

indicators.note: first tells us the finished part comes before the story

parts.note: over means finished
a lie is a story, a falsehood

explanation.surface: A cover story was finished before anything else.
explanation.definitionFit: To overlie is to lie on top of something and so cover it.

clue.text: Revolutionary France's memorial banner

indicators.note: revolutionary suggests turning the letters over into a new arrangement

parts.note: F is the international abbreviation for France

explanation.surface: A memorial of revolutionary France takes the form of a flag.
explanation.definitionFit: The oriflamme was the red banner of the French kings, later any battle standard.

clue.text: Town where one enthusiast stifles resistance to another

indicators.note: stifles means smothers, so the first piece encloses the second

parts.note: a fan is an enthusiast
R is the symbol for electrical resistance
another enthusiast: a ham is an amateur radio enthusiast

explanation.surface: In some town a fan suppresses opposition to a fellow devotee.
explanation.walkthrough: A ham is an amateur radio enthusiast. Farnham is a town in Surrey, England.
explanation.definitionFit: Farnham is a market town in Surrey, south-west of London.

clue.text: Parent taking long and lyrical measure

indicators.note: taking means taking in, so the parent holds the other piece

parts.note: mum is a parent, British for mom
odic means of an ode, a long lyrical poem

explanation.surface: A mother takes a lengthy, poetic measure.
explanation.definitionFit: A modicum is a small amount or measure of something.

clue.text: The admiral's in the hold

definitions.meaning: Horatio ..., victor at Trafalgar, the most famous British admiral
a wrestling hold applied from behind

explanation.definitionFit: Nelson is Britain's famous admiral and also a wrestling grip on the neck.

clue.text: Providing a reminder to observe fast again?

parts.note: re- is a prefix meaning again
to do a fast is to observe it
Lent is the Christian season of fasting

explanation.surface: A question about whether repeating a fast serves as a reminder.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as RE-DO LENT: to keep the Lenten fast again.
explanation.definitionFit: Redolent means strongly suggestive or reminiscent of something.

clue.text: Military operations drowning piano passage with strong current

indicators.note: drowning means submerging, so the piano goes inside the operations

parts.note: raids are military operations
p is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly

explanation.surface: Soldiers' raids drown out a piano piece with a forceful flow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'piano passage' looks like a musical phrase but splits: P, then the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Rapids are a stretch of river where the water flows fast and turbulently.

clue.text: Flower-like oeuvre of Britney Spears?

definitions.meaning: a red-flowered field plant, emblem of remembrance
Britney Spears's songs are pop music, so they are pop-like

explanation.surface: A singer's songs are compared to a bloom.
explanation.definitionFit: Poppy names a flower and, jokingly, describes music in the pop style.

clue.text: Head of Broadcasting wants to broadcast "Legend of the Forge Master"

indicators.note: head of means the first letter of the word that follows

parts.note: lacks means wants, is without

indicators.note: a broadcast is heard, so this signals a word that sounds like another

parts.note: a myth is a legend

explanation.surface: A broadcasting chief plans to air a legend about a master of the forge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to broadcast' says MYTH is heard as MITH. 'broadcast' appears twice, once inside the first letter's word.
explanation.definitionFit: A blacksmith is a craftsman who works iron at a forge.

clue.text: 16 pints producing cursory display of affection

definitions.meaning: a dry measure of two gallons, i.e. sixteen pints

explanation.definitionFit: A peck is an old two-gallon measure and also a brief kiss.

clue.text: Stickler taking name of dangler

indicators.note: taking in, so the stickler holds the name inside

parts.note: a pedant is a stickler for rules

explanation.surface: A fussy person takes the name of something hanging down.
explanation.definitionFit: A pendant is a hanging ornament, something that dangles.

clue.text: Austen heroine embraces Peake hero at noxious gathering

indicators.note: embraces means holds within, so the heroine wraps around the hero

parts.note: Emma is the title heroine of Jane Austen's novel
Mr Pye is the title character of Mervyn Peake's novel

explanation.surface: One literary heroine hugs another author's hero at an unpleasant get-together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gathering' is medical: a collection of pus. Mervyn Peake wrote 'Mr Pye'.
explanation.definitionFit: Empyema is a collection of pus in a body cavity, a noxious accumulation.
